To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of low frequency ultrasonic irradiation with glass beads (GB) and single-wall carbon nanotubes SWNTs) enhanced the removal of the pharmaceuticals ibuprofen (IPB) and sulfamethylazol (SMX).
the combination of glass beads (0.1-10gL(-1)) and single-walled CNTs (0-45mgL(- 1)) at 28kHz enhanced the removal of ibuprofen (94%) and sulfamethazole (88%) by ultrasound.
the degradation of the pharmaceuticals IBP and SMZ in aqueous solutions was enhanced using ultrasonic irradiation in the presence of both GBs and SWNs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degradation of pharmaceuticals using low frequency ultrasound in the presence of different types of catalysts.
the use of glass beads and SWNTs to improve the removal of IBP, a common non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, and SMX, a widely used sulfonamide antibiotic, in aqueous solution.
the removal of pharmaceuticals from wastewater using low frequency sonocatalytic processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of GBs/SWNTs with ultrasonic irradiation at 28kHz would be the most efficient technique for the removal of IBP/SMX from aqueous solutions.
the use of GBs and the combination of GBs/SWNTs in a sonochemical reactor can be used as an effective method to degrade pharmaceuticals.
the combination of GBs (10gL(-1) and SWNTs (0.05mgL(-1)) at the low frequency is the most effective for the removal of both IBP and MX.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of catalysts (GBs and SWNT) with low ultrasonic frequencies (e.g., 28kHz) is a suitable and effective approach for the degradation of pharmaceuticals.
the use of GBs and/or SWNTs as catalysts in combination with low ultrasonic frequencies is a suitable technique to enhance the sonochemical degradation of pharmaceuticals in water.
the degradation of IBP and sulfamethaxazole was enhanced by GBs and SWCNTs, which is due to the increase of the OH radical production and the adsorption of the target pollutants on the catalysts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of GBs (as a source of OH radicals) and SWNTs (as a catalyst for the degradation) can enhance the degradation of IBP and the SMX at the low ultrasonic frequency.
the use of catalysts can be an alternative for wastewater treatment.
the use of GBs and/or SWNTs can be used to enhance the degradation of IBP and/or SMX by ultrasonic irradiation.
